Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

An optoelectronic assembly and method for operating an optoelectronic assembly are provided herein. The optoelectronic assembly may include an organic light-emitting component, a temperature sensor for recording a temperature value, and a controller coupled to the organic light-emitting component and to the temperature sensor. The controller may be configured to apply an alternating current (AC) voltage to the organic light-emitting component when the organic light-emitting component is switched on, and if the recorded temperature value is less than a predetermined temperature threshold value, where the AC voltage may, at least, temporarily less than an instantaneous threshold voltage of the organic light-emitting component. The controller may also be configured to apply a direct current (DC) voltage to the organic light-emitting component if a measurement value is greater than or equal to a predetermined threshold value, where the DC voltage is greater than the instantaneous threshold voltage of the organic light-emitting component.

outputs.L2: Disclosed are an optoelectronic assembly and a technique for controlling its operation. The assembly can comprise an organic light-emitting element, a temperature sensor that detects a temperature value, and a controller connected to both the sensor and the light-emitting element. When the organic light-emitting element is activated and the detected temperature is below a predefined temperature limit, the controller can supply the element with an alternating-current (AC) voltage. This AC voltage may, at least for a limited period, be lower than the element’s instantaneous threshold voltage. The controller can further supply a direct-current (DC) voltage when a measured value reaches or exceeds a specified threshold. The optoelectronic assembly comprises an organic light-emitting component, a temperature sensor, and a controller. The temperature sensor measures and records a temperature value associated with the assembly.

When the organic light-emitting component is switched on and the recorded temperature is below a predetermined temperature threshold, the controller applies an alternating-current (AC) voltage to the component. During this operation, the applied AC voltage may temporarily fall below the instantaneous threshold voltage of the organic light-emitting component.

If a measured value reaches or exceeds a predetermined threshold, the controller instead applies a direct-current (DC) voltage that is greater than the component’s instantaneous threshold voltage.
outputs.L4:
An optoelectronic assembly includes an organic light-emitting component, a temperature sensor thermally coupled to or positioned near the component, and a controller configured to regulate the voltage supplied to the component. During operation, the temperature sensor measures the temperature of the organic light-emitting component or its surrounding environment and provides a corresponding signal to the controller. The controller compares the measured temperature with a predetermined temperature threshold and may also evaluate one or more electrical, optical, temporal, or sensor-derived measurements against associated qualification thresholds.

When the measured temperature is below the predetermined temperature threshold, the controller temporarily applies an alternating-current voltage to the organic light-emitting component. The magnitude of this AC voltage remains below the component’s instantaneous threshold voltage, such that the component is not continuously driven in its normal light-emitting state. The AC voltage may be applied for a selected interval or until the temperature or another monitored parameter satisfies a specified condition.

If a monitored measurement meets the applicable qualification criterion, the controller switches to or enables a direct-current operating mode. In this mode, the controller applies a DC voltage having a magnitude greater than the instantaneous threshold voltage of the organic light-emitting component, thereby causing or supporting light emission. The controller may repeatedly evaluate the temperature and other measurements and transition between the AC and DC modes as operating conditions change. In this way, the assembly provides temperature-responsive control of the organic light-emitting component while accounting for changes in its instantaneous threshold voltage and measured operating state.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest yet most frequently used words in the English language. Known as the definite article, it identifies a particular person, place, object, or idea. For example, “a book” can mean any book, while “the book” refers to a specific one.

Although it appears simple, “the” brings clarity and precision to communication. It helps readers understand what is already known, unique, or important in a sentence. Without it, everyday language would often sound incomplete or confusing.

This tiny word demonstrates how even the simplest parts of language can have a significant impact.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for an optoelectronic assembly that controls an organic light-emitting component using temperature-dependent AC and DC voltages.
counterfactuals.output: An optoelectronic assembly includes an organic light-emitting component, a temperature sensor configured to determine a temperature associated with the organic light-emitting component, and a driver circuit electrically coupled to the organic light-emitting component. The driver circuit supplies a drive signal comprising an alternating-current voltage component and a direct-current voltage component. A controller receives temperature information from the temperature sensor and adjusts at least one characteristic of the alternating-current voltage component and at least one characteristic of the direct-current voltage component as a function of the determined temperature. The adjusted characteristics may include amplitude, frequency, duty cycle, waveform, polarity, or DC bias level. The controller may select the characteristics according to stored temperature-dependent operating parameters or a feedback control algorithm. Temperature-dependent control of the alternating-current and direct-current voltage components compensates for changes in electrical and optical behavior of the organic light-emitting component, thereby improving emission stability, efficiency, uniformity, and operating lifetime over a range of temperatures.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an OLED device and operating method in which a controller uses a temperature sensor to select between alternating-current and direct-current driving modes based on predetermined thresholds.
counterfactuals.output:
An OLED device includes an OLED panel, a temperature sensor, a drive circuit capable of both direct-current (DC) and alternating-current (AC) operation, and a controller. The sensor detects the panel or ambient temperature and supplies a corresponding signal to the controller.

The controller compares the detected temperature with one or more predetermined temperature thresholds stored in memory. Depending on the temperature range, it selects a predefined drive mode:

- **DC mode:** the OLED pixels are driven with substantially constant polarity during emission.
- **AC mode:** the applied pixel voltage or current periodically changes polarity, typically alternating between a forward-emission interval and a reverse- or non-emission-bias interval.

Two thresholds may be used to provide hysteresis. For example, the controller changes from DC mode to AC mode when the temperature crosses a first threshold, but does not return to DC mode until the temperature crosses a second threshold in the opposite direction. This avoids repeated mode switching when the measured temperature fluctuates near a boundary. The particular temperature range assigned to each mode may be fixed during manufacture or stored as programmable calibration data.

The operating method therefore comprises sensing temperature, comparing it with the predetermined threshold or thresholds, selecting the corresponding AC or DC driving algorithm, and controlling the panel driver accordingly. Temperature may be monitored continuously or periodically so that the driving mode can be changed during operation, thereby balancing power consumption, image quality, and OLED lifetime.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise technical summary of an invention involving an organic light-emitting component, a temperature sensor, and a controller that applies AC voltage at low temperatures and DC voltage when a measurement reaches a threshold.
counterfactuals.output: An organic light-emitting device includes an organic light-emitting component, a temperature sensor, and a controller. At temperatures below a predetermined threshold, the controller applies an AC voltage to the component to support low-temperature operation. When the sensed temperature reaches or exceeds the threshold, the controller switches to DC voltage for normal light emission.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate patent claim-like language for an optoelectronic assembly whose controller temporarily applies an AC voltage below the OLED’s instantaneous threshold voltage, then applies a DC voltage above that threshold under a specified condition.
counterfactuals.output:
1. **An optoelectronic assembly comprising:**

   an organic light-emitting diode (OLED) having an instantaneous threshold voltage;

   a voltage source electrically coupled to the OLED; and

   a controller operatively coupled to the voltage source and configured to:

   cause the voltage source, during a first operating interval, to apply across the OLED an alternating-current voltage having a peak magnitude less than the instantaneous threshold voltage of the OLED; and

   in response to satisfaction of a specified condition, cause the voltage source, during a second operating interval subsequent to the first operating interval, to apply across the OLED a direct-current voltage having a magnitude greater than the instantaneous threshold voltage.

2. **The optoelectronic assembly of claim 1**, wherein the specified condition comprises expiration of a predetermined duration of the first operating interval.

3. **The optoelectronic assembly of claim 1**, further comprising a sensing circuit configured to determine an electrical characteristic of the OLED, wherein the specified condition comprises the electrical characteristic satisfying a threshold criterion.

4. **The optoelectronic assembly of claim 3**, wherein the electrical characteristic comprises at least one of an impedance, a capacitance, a leakage current, a phase response, or a temperature associated with the OLED.

5. **The optoelectronic assembly of claim 1**, wherein the controller is configured to determine or estimate the instantaneous threshold voltage based on at least one of temperature, operating history, aging, measured current, or measured impedance of the OLED.

6. **The optoelectronic assembly of claim 1**, wherein the alternating-current voltage is insufficient to cause substantial light emission by the OLED, and the direct-current voltage causes the OLED to emit light.

7. **The optoelectronic assembly of claim 1**, wherein the alternating-current voltage comprises a bipolar waveform having substantially zero time-averaged voltage.

8. **A method of operating an optoelectronic assembly including an OLED, the method comprising:**

   determining or estimating an instantaneous threshold voltage of the OLED;

   temporarily applying across the OLED an alternating-current voltage having a peak magnitude below the instantaneous threshold voltage;

   determining that a specified condition has been satisfied; and

   in response to determining that the specified condition has been satisfied, applying across the OLED a direct-current voltage having a magnitude above the instantaneous threshold voltage.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Create an abstract for a temperature-controlled OLED startup system designed to improve low-temperature operation by switching between sub-threshold AC excitation and above-threshold DC driving.
counterfactuals.output: **Abstract—** Organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) exhibit increased impedance, delayed turn-on, and reduced luminance at low temperatures because of suppressed carrier mobility and injection. This work presents a temperature-controlled startup system that combines sub-threshold alternating-current (AC) excitation with conventional above-threshold direct-current (DC) driving. During cold startup, a temperature sensor and feedback controller apply a bounded AC waveform below the OLED’s light-emission threshold, enabling controlled electrical preconditioning and internal heating while limiting visible flicker, excessive current, and localized stress. Once the measured temperature, impedance, or estimated junction state reaches a predefined transition criterion, the controller switches to regulated above-threshold DC operation and ramps the drive level to the target luminance. Protection functions constrain peak voltage, current, temperature, and startup duration under abnormal conditions. The proposed dual-mode strategy improves low-temperature turn-on stability, shortens luminance-settling time, and reduces the electrical overstress associated with immediate high-voltage DC startup. It is suitable for OLED displays and lighting systems used in automotive, aerospace, outdoor, and other cold-environment applications.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
